label: Pre-copy steps (t>=2 through <DEL>) of sequences starting with p/k (also m, r, b, 1)
explanation: Sequence-level context feature. It fires only in the original phase from t=2 onward and at the <DEL> step, with about 99% of its mass there. It is silent at t=0-1 and almost silent in the copy phase, apart from a weak tail at the first one or two copy steps. Whether it fires, and how strongly, depends on the first original tokens. First token p gives the most: 42% of its pre-copy steps are active, with 95% precision when restricted to t>=2, and these steps hold most of the top activation quartile. k comes next, then m, r, b and 1. A p or k at position 1 also turns it on. Activation peaks around t=3-5 and at <DEL>, and in the top examples it stays high through the whole input. Sequences that begin with other letters (a, s, etc.) give only weak, scattered activations, which make up most of the misses. The feature does not depend on the current input token or on L. The predicate captures 81% of activation mass on dev, but precision is about 0.47 because many sequences that start with these tokens get no activation.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the first original token (most: p, k, m, r, 1, b; least: x, w, e, c) and the second original token (most: p, k, 1, r, a, q; least: v, x, w, e); timing cues that raise it most: t=4, t=5, t=3.
